summary: An L-4 lookout cab on Horse Mountain in Lane County was built in 1932 and gone by 1965; no source describes what remains on the summit.

facts.status_note: Cab gone since 1965; no source describes what remains on the summit.

events.note: Burros and packers to carry two lookout houses, Horse Mountain among the summits; material on the ground by September
14x14 L-4 gable-roof lookout house per the Weebly history; register gives the 1932 L-4 cab
A retired railroad man and his wife were to man the lookout, per the Register-Guard
Register and Weebly history say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, May 8, 2011

notes_for_editor: Fate conflict: the register and the Weebly history say removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965. The story reports both. The register calls the site a ground lookout; no source gives a height or structure size beyond the 14x14 house. The record's material 'wood' is inferred from the L-4 design and no source states it; a human should check it. Access, staffing beyond 1948, and what remains today are not described by any source. Two web searches found no other Horse Mountain lookout in the Willamette or Cascade forests; a summit named Horse Mountain in Josephine County came up in results but was not used. Photos on the FFLOS record (1946, Howard Verschoor collection) were not re-checked and are not added here.
